CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. James is a 42-year-old female presenting with a right index finger injury sustained while skiing on double black diamond slopes this past Saturday, approximately 5 days ago. She reports losing control while skiing downhill, flipping several times, and jamming her index finger on an object during the fall. She denies other injuries. Pain is rated 7/10. She attempted ibuprofen for pain management without significant relief. She has not used ice or a splint prior to this visit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reviewed and otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic constipation
2. Appendectomy at age 7

MEDICATIONS
1. Miralax for chronic constipation
2. Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, for current injury)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand x-ray reviewed: Normal; all joints and bones in correct position; no fractures identified. Physical examination of the right index finger reveals tenderness to palpation, pain with traction, and pain with squeezing over the distal interphalangeal joint.

RESULTS
X-ray, right hand: No fractures; normal study.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger. Plan: (1) Splint application to right index finger; (2) Mobic 15 mg orally once daily, dispense 14 tablets; (3) Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine need for hand therapy.
